source.title: Comparing Detection, Treatment, Outcomes, and Spending for Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Between MA and FFS
source.location: Results narrative: FFS chronic diabetes post-index inpatient ~13%; diabetes-principal IP rare (~0.6%)
source.citation: Avalere Health. Comparing Detection, Treatment, Outcomes, and Spending for Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Between MA and FFS (2023 white paper).

population.enrollment_notes: Source compares matched MA/FFS; this finding uses the FFS chronic diabetes inpatient figure only.

cohort.inclusion_notes: FFS beneficiaries with chronic diabetes; post-index inpatient utilization.
cohort.exclusion_notes: MA comparison arm not used; diabetes-principal admissions are not the estimand.

numerator.notes: Approximates all-cause IP claim presence (MVP O1), not diabetes-principal IP.

estimand.notes: P(O1 = 1 | diabetes) crude risk among Option-B eligible.

analysis.notes: Industry white paper; not peer-reviewed CMS. Used as weak utilization prior with explicit grade B.

result.notes: Scouting magnitude ~13% FFS chronic diabetes post-index IP from Phase 0 inventory / Avalere narrative.

assumptions: All-cause IP presence approximates the source post-index inpatient utilization construct.
Industry report accepted only as a weak calibration prior with documented caveats.

governance.rationale: Accepted as calibration target #3 (utilization) because no cleaner public O1-compatible official aggregate was pinned; grade B and gaps retained. Prefer replacement if a 2021 FFS all-cause IP-among-diabetes official extract is later pinned.
